This is impacting our customer-facing scheduling flow — several customers reported failures. We have sample request/response logs and a few stack traces (attached).

Subject: Ascend performance incident — immediate mitigations & next steps

Priya — thank you for joining the 10:30 PT bridge. Short status update and what we did:

What we observed (during 04:30–08:15 UTC):
- Elevated tail latency from a specific model variant (variant-3-quant) following a configuration tweak pushed 02:50 UTC.
- Autoscaler showed transient GPU queueing; several requests timed out and were retried, compounding load.

Actions taken (completed):
- Rolled back the micro-change to the quant metadata for Ascend traffic at 11:05 PT (immediate rollback).
- Temporarily pinned Ascend to variant-2-stable while we validate performance under production load.
- Increased KV cache TTL for Ascend sessions to reduce recomputation for repeated prefixes.
- Architected short-term concurrency cap to avoid queue buildup; applied as a conservative setting for the next 4 hours.

Immediate impact: error rate dropped from ~7% to ~0.8% within 35 minutes after rollback; median latency is trending back toward baseline (1.9s). We will continue to monitor for the next 4 hours.

Next steps:
- Connor/Eng to complete a focused RCA and publish a 24-hour initial report to the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/INC-20270503 by EOD PT.
- We’ll hold a 30-minute follow-up at 15:00 PT for validation and discuss permanent remediation.
- I’ll send a short exec-level summary to Ascend and coordinate any contractual remediation (credits) with finance if needed.

Can you confirm receipt and whether Ascend needs a written timeline for a credit/contract follow-up? We will also share the initial-rca-outline-20270503.docx after Connor populates the technical timeline.

Appreciate the quick coordination —
Rishi Malhotra
